Subject: Dedicated capacity: autoscaling & throughput sizing follow-up

Hi Samir -

Thanks again for the call earlier - great overview of Acme's roadmap and traffic patterns. Quick recap + a few follow-ups so we can size Dedicated capacity and plan the technical deep dive: 

Call recap (high level):
- Workloads: customer-facing chat (streaming responses) + small synchronous reranker (top-K re-rank) + periodic batch embeddings pipeline.
- Current traffic (observed): baseline ~40-60 req/s, expected steady growth to ~120-150 req/s during peak campaigns; occasional spikes up to ~250 req/s for 10-15 minute windows.
- Typical request size: chat context ~512 tokens avg, responses ~128-512 tokens (streaming preferred). Embedding calls are smaller (single text vectors ~768 dims).
- Latency SLOs: p95 < 300ms for chat turn completions (streaming acceptable), reranker latency <= 150ms for top-10.
- Security: must support VPC peering or private link; prefer token-based auth with mutual TLS optional for Private deployment.

Open questions we flagged on the call:
1) Preferred auth path for Private (mTLS vs token + private link)?
2) Do you expect synchronous rerank at request time for >100 qps or will you do candidate generation offline and re-rank fewer items online?
3) Any strict limits on queue depth / acceptable queuing latency during bursts?

What we need from you to finalize sizing:
- Confirm peak concurrency (requests/sec) for synchronous reranks and chat (best guess for Q4).
- Any hard P95 targets stricter than we captured.

Next steps:
- I've attached a Dedicated sizing worksheet and a mutual action plan. Please fill in the traffic & business constraints column - that will let us produce a recommended instance profile (min/max instances, burst capacity, queue sizing, and autoscale rules).
- Technical deep-dive (runtime + routing + auth): propose Tue 30 Aug 2026, 10:00-11:00 PT. Aditya (cc) will take the lead on kernel/concurrency sizing.

Cc'ing Aditya for technical notes below - Aditya, feel free to add specifics on concurrency per-GPU and batching suggestions.

Thanks -

Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa - good summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we fill the worksheet: 

1) Reranker: we'll likely run a hybrid approach. Most queries will use a fast approximate candidate set from our vector DB (Faiss) and then a synchronous re-rank for top 20 candidates at request time for high-value flows (we expect ~30-50 req/s for rerank during peak).

2) Auth: for now we'd prefer token-based auth over a private link (we want to avoid networking changes during PoC). If we move to Private later, mTLS is fine.

3) Queue/backpressure: we can tolerate up to ~2s additional queuing latency during brief spikes, but anything beyond 5s will be unacceptable. We'd like automatic burst capacity for very short spikes (under 5 minutes).

4) For model sizing: we expect to use an off-the-shelf quantized 13B model for chat in PoC and may move to a 70B quantized model later for higher-quality responses. Any guidance on per-GPU concurrency for 13B vs 70B would help our capacity planning.

We'll fill the worksheet with conservative Q4 estimates by EOD Thu and confirm the 30 Aug slot if Aditya is available.

 - Samir
VP Product, Acme Labs
samir@acmelabs.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: autoscaling & throughput sizing follow-up

Hey team -

A few technical notes to help with the worksheet and the deep-dive. These are conservative, productized recommendations based on our runtime benchmarks and similar customer workloads. Exact numbers will vary by model, quantization, and hardware.

Autoscaling triggers & cooldowns:
- Primary autoscale metric: tokens_in_flight (recommended) or GPU_utilization if tokens are hard to measure in your stack.
- Cooldown: 60s for scale-up, 180s for scale-down (to avoid oscillation on short spikes).
- Min instances: 2 (for redundancy), burst reserve: +3 instances for very short spikes, Max instances: set per contract (we typically suggest start with 20 and iterate).

Per-instance concurrency guidance (example on A100 80GB or similar):
- 13B quant (8-bit): ~20-30 concurrent lightweight chat requests at 512 tokens (avg response ~256 tokens) with p95 < 250ms when using streaming + batching.
- 70B quant (8-bit or 4-bit): ~6-10 concurrent requests at 512 tokens with p95 in the 250-400ms range; plan for lower concurrency and rely more on batching.

Batching & queuing recommendations:
- Dynamic batching: enable up to batch_size 32 for CPU/GPU fusion where it improves throughput; prefer latency-aware batching that caps per-batch latency at ~40-60ms.
- Queue depth: soft queue limit per cluster: ~1,000 requests (with priority routing to reduce tail latency for high-value flows). Hard cap: 5,000 requests (backpressure + 429s).
- Backpressure policy: return 429 when queue depth > hard cap; send Retry-After header with suggested cooldown; for Private/Dedicated we can also route overflow to a fallback, lower-cost model.

Routing & fallbacks:
- Smart routing: tag critical flows (payment/checkout) to priority queue and reserve min instances to keep p95 SLOs.
- Fallbacks: automatically route to a smaller quantized model variant when queue depth is high; maintain consistency in structured output by using same tool-calling schema across variants.

Auth & SDK notes:
- Auth: token-based JWT is simplest for PoC; for Private deployments we recommend mTLS + token for defense-in-depth.
- SDKs: Redwood Python/Node SDKs support streaming, structured output, and tool-calling. Use the routed_endpoint param for Dedicated capacity to avoid extra hop through the public API.

Embeddings & rerankers:
- Offline embeddings: batch to S3 (or your DB), index nightly.
- Online rerank: expect 30-50 synchronous rerank QPS to require dedicated instances (we recommend separating rerank service from chat pool so one can be tuned aggressively for short p95s).
- Hybrid approach: do candidate retrieval with Faiss, then rerank top 20 synchronously. Reranker model should be small/efficient binary (like a tuned 2-4B) to keep p95s under 150ms.

Suggested initial config for PoC (conservative):
- Chat pool (13B quant): min 2 instances, max 12, burst +3, concurrency limit per instance 20.
- Rerank pool (small 2-4B): min 1 instance, max 6, concurrency limit per instance 50.
- Autoscale on tokens_in_flight with the cooldowns above.

I'll bring detailed benchmark plots and a sample autoscale policy to the 30 Aug deep-dive.

 - Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com
